genesis.39.p1.b1.text: Meanwhile, Joseph had been taken down to Egypt, where an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.

genesis.39.p1.b2.text: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, serving in the household of his Egyptian master.

genesis.39.p1.b3.text: When his master saw that the LORD was with him and made him prosper in all he did,

genesis.39.p2.b1.text: Potiphar put him in charge of his household and entrusted him with everything he owned.

genesis.39.p2.b2.text: … the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s household on account of him. The LORD’s blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field.

genesis.39.p2.b3.text: … he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate.

genesis.39.p2.b4.text: Now Joseph was well-built and handsome

genesis.39.p3.b1.text: … after some time his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph …

genesis.39.p3.b3.text: Look … with me here, my master does not concern himself with anything in his house, and he has entrusted everything he owns to my care. … He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife.

genesis.39.p3.b4.text: So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?

genesis.39.p3.b5.text: Although Potiphar’s wife spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be near her.

genesis.39.p4.b1.text: One day, however, Joseph went into the house to attend to his work, and not a single household servant was inside.

genesis.39.p4.b3.text: But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.

genesis.39.p5.b1.text: When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,

genesis.39.p5.b2.text: Look … this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us.

genesis.39.p5.b3.text: So Potiphar’s wife kept Joseph’s cloak beside her until his master came home.

genesis.39.p5.b4.text: The Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me, but when I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.

genesis.39.p6.b1.text: When his master heard the story his wife told him … he burned with anger.

genesis.39.p6.b2.text: So Joseph’s master took him and had him thrown into the prison where the king’s prisoners were confined.

genesis.39.p6.b3.text: While Joseph was there in the prison

genesis.39.p7.b1.text: the LORD was with him and extended kindness to him, granting him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.

genesis.39.p7.b2.text: And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care …

genesis.39.p7.b3.text: … because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.
